why.label: Why datixxia™
why.lead: datixxia™ turns published public contract award data into accessible economic intelligence. Explore recorded award values, changes in activity and the distribution of awards across sectors and suppliers to support business decisions, research and investigations.

cards.title: Patterns in procurement
cards.text: The platform draws on historical records and incoming award notices to reveal patterns in public procurement across sectors and suppliers.

cards.title: Visibility into future periods
cards.text: Where records include reliable contract dates and durations, they can help users examine commitments extending into future periods.

cards.title: Evidence, not guarantees
cards.text: These insights reflect the available contract data; they are not guarantees of future spending or measures of the entire economy. The first program specification was filed with INPI under reference DSO2023020065 in December 2023.

about.label: About
about.title: Facts for futures™
about.text:
Every business decision involves a view of the future. Whether planning investment, allocating resources or exploring a new market, organisations need evidence to understand where activity is developing and what it could mean for them.

Public contract awards provide part of that evidence: purchases already awarded, the suppliers selected and, where disclosed, the values and periods involved. datixxia™ makes this information easier to explore and interpret — helping users examine market activity, follow changes and identify potential opportunities.

model.label: Model
model.title: The datixxia™ Intelligence Model
model.lead: Public procurement supports activity across infrastructure, transport, energy, education, health and many other sectors. Awarded contracts identify selected suppliers and can generate demand for subcontractors, materials and services — revealing patterns of economic activity and potential opportunities across supply chains.

team.label: Team
team.title: Our team
team.intro: Built by operators who understand data and public markets

members.name: Malcolm Duff
members.bio:
Malcolm founded and led the first translation company in France to obtain ISO 9001 certification and was chief technology translator for UNESCO in Paris. He originated the concept behind datixxia™ and developed its foundations through research into how public contract award data can support economic intelligence and business decisions.

His experience includes coordinating international projects with translators from 33 countries through Inttranet™, included in the UNESCO Observatory on the Information Society in January 2006. At DataTixx, he leads company strategy, partnership development and the preparation of datixxia™ for commercial launch.

members.name: Yana Levchenko
members.bio:
The founder of her own web design company only one year after escaping from the war in Ukraine with her children and pets, Yana has extensive experience in cyber-security and computing, backed by wide-ranging skills in web design for a fast-growing customer base.

She also brings to the team her eye for detail and aesthetic sense of beauty as a professional photographer published in magazines worldwide. As Managing Director, she works alongside Malcolm to develop DataTixx and prepare datixxia™ for its users.

faq.title: FAQs
faq.lead: Direct answers to the questions we hear most often from the terminal floor.

items.a: No. datixxia™ uses zero artificial intelligence or statistical extrapolation. We read only signed, legally binding procurement contracts that remain valid for years.
We ingest public and private contract award notices from 194 countries daily. Every data point is a real buyer, a real supplier, and a real committed value.

items.q: How far ahead do you forecast?
items.a: Our patent-pending cascade model produces verifiable four-year forecasts. Each projection is anchored to a source document you can check yourself.
We offer a Free tier to explore the terminal. Standard is €100 and Premium is €200 per user per month for full access to indexes and forecasts.
